old_claims.statement: At each fixed bounded smooth positive multiplier, the closed Dolbeault differential domains, kernels, ranges and exactness are preserved, and compactly supported smooth sections are form cores on the specified complete orbifold, without identifying weighted and unweighted adjoint domains.
old_claims.attribution: Standard equivalent-norm and complete Hilbert-complex arguments; expanded by old Argus proof.md Section 2 from the compact manuscript domain discussion.
old_claims.supported_scope: Fixed-parameter equivalence and inherited exactness/closed ranges; complete smooth finite-chart orbifold form cores with no global bound on derivatives of h.

hypotheses: The original complex is a closed complete Dolbeault Hilbert complex with a common positive unweighted form gap delta.
The fixed smooth scalar multiplier satisfies 1<=h<=B<infinity in each degree.
The lifted orbifold metric is complete; finite invariant charts permit local smoothing.
supported_scope: Equality of maximal and minimal differential-domain sets under equivalent graph norms.
Inheritance of closed images and exactness from the unweighted complex.
Unweighted primitives of norm at most delta^(-1/2) and coarse weighted minimal inverse norm at most sqrt(B/delta).
Complete-domain form cores for Dom d intersect Dom d_h^*, even when derivatives of h are not globally bounded.
limitations: Equivalent norms alone do not prove exactness of an arbitrary complex.
Weighted and unweighted adjoint domains need not agree and are not asserted to agree.
The cutoff proof depends on completeness and is not an incomplete-domain result.
No scalar compiler or rational calculation certifies these analytic facts.

prior_review_reconciliation.interpretation: Same-subject historical prose support; pending graph labels and current acceptance are separate.

decisive_checks: Graph-norm equivalence applies to the differential and its degreewise output, not to an unchanged adjoint.
The unweighted form gap proves closed images and exactness by orthogonal minimal lifts.
Cutoff commutators eliminate metric-potential derivatives, followed by compact local smoothing of the joint first-order system.
